## Why this revision exists

WM1 measured the whole project — 90 items in 10 sections — and carried **no
rate anywhere in it**. That was deliberate, and the master says why (Part G):

> *Rates come from the MES SSR. No item number could be verified from the
> material available, and inventing one would put false authority on a document
> an executing engineer might rely on.*

The project owner has now supplied the schedule itself: **`SSR 22-23 MH (1).pdf`**,
624 pages, the Government of Maharashtra Public Works Department State Schedule
of Rates for 2022-23, approved by Government Circular RADASU-2022/PR.KR.12/
NIYOJAN-3 dated 25 July 2022 and effective from that date. Every item number can
now be verified, so the bill can be priced. That is all WM4 does.

## The three things the schedule itself settled

### 1. Overheads and profit are already in the rate — so they are not added again

The SSR General Notes are explicit:

> *For labour amenities and all other overhead charges, **10 % provision is
> considered in Rate Abstract**. In addition, **10 % provision for Contractor's
> Profit** is also considered separately.*
> *Labour Cess at **1 %** has been considered separately in Rate Abstracts.*

The owner's own estimate adds **10 % contractor's overhead and profit** on top
of its rates. Against SSR completed rates that would be a double count, and WM4
does not make it. The on-cost already inside every rate is
1.10 × 1.10 × 1.01 = **1.2221**, and the same factor is what carries a
derived material difference into a derived rate.

### 2. Formwork is already in the concrete rate — so F-01 and F-02 are not payable

Every SSR concrete item reads *"including **steel centering, formwork**, cover
blocks ... **(excluding reinforcement and structural steel)**"*. So the
1 057.743 m² of formwork and the 104 m² of falsework stay in the bill as
measured control figures at **nil**, and reinforcement is billed separately at
SSR 26.33. The 14-day prop period on the pressure slab remains a **programme**
driver whether or not it is a payable item.

The same logic retires three other groups from the money column: the bricks,
cement and sand of the sentry masonry are inside SSR 27.05; the cement and
aggregate procurement volumes are inside every composite rate; and **item W-05
and item B-screed are the same protection screed measured twice**, once in m²
and once in m³ — 102.889 × 0.100 = 10.289. It is paid once.

### 3. A grade the schedule does not publish is derived by the schedule's own rule

The SSR publishes R.C.C. **pardi** (wall) and staircase **waist slab** only to
M-25. The shelter box is M-35. The SSR says what to do:

> *If higher Concrete grade is required for any specific work, the rate analysis
> of the same shall be derived by **adding difference in standard cement
> consumption** in relevant SSR item's rate and shall be got approved from the
> Superintending Engineer, PWD of concerned circle.*

Standard consumption, from the SSR's own table: M25 **7.50** bags/m³,
M30 **8.00**, M35 **8.25**. Cement at the SSR general rate ₹6 000/M.T.

**And the formula is checked against the schedule before it is trusted.** Where
the SSR *does* publish consecutive grades, the step it prints must equal what
the formula computes — and it does, in four separate item families:

| Step | Formula | What the SSR prints |
|---|---:|---|
| M20 → M25 | 183.32 | 183 / 184 |
| M25 → M30 | 183.32 | 183 / 184 |
| M30 → M35 | 91.66 | 91 / 92 |

So the M-35 wall rate is ₹15,750 + ₹275 = **₹16,024.97/m³**, and the
M-35 staircase rate ₹12,244 + ₹275 = **₹12,518.97/m³**.

## The excavation, priced by depth band

The SSR General Notes carry an increase for building excavation below 3.0 m:
**3.0–4.5 m add 20 %**, **4.5–6.0 m add 30 %**, and *"depth beyond 6.0 m — extra
percent to be decided by concerned Superintending Engineer."*

The shelter goes to **(−)6.800**. So the bulk excavation is billed in six bands
rather than as one line, and the bands reproduce the WM1 quantities exactly:

| Band | Strata | m³ | SSR | Rate ₹/m³ |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| 0.000 to (-)1.500 | soil | 295.20 | 21.02 | 207.00 |
| (-)1.500 to (-)1.750 | soil | 49.20 | 21.04 | 258.00 |
| (-)1.750 to (-)3.000 | Deccan basalt | 246.00 | 21.20 | 1,307.00 |
| (-)3.000 to (-)4.500 | Deccan basalt | 295.20 | 21.20 | 1,568.40 |
| (-)4.500 to (-)6.000 | Deccan basalt | 295.20 | 21.20 | 1,699.10 |
| (-)6.000 to (-)6.800 | Deccan basalt | 157.44 | 21.20 | 1,699.10 |

Soil 295.20 + 49.20 = **344.40**, against WM1 item E-02a's 344.4.
Rock 246.00 + 295.20 + 295.20 + 157.44 = **993.84**, against WM1 item E-02b's
993.84. Nothing is re-measured; the same volume is simply billed where the
schedule says it should be.

**The rock is broken, not blasted.** `WM_CONSTRUCTION_METHODOLOGY.md` and risk
`S-02` both say so: *"Rock is removed by HYDRAULIC BREAKER, not by blasting ...
controlled blasting would require a vibration regime the project has not
specified."* So **SSR 21.20**, the schedule's chiselling / wedging / line
drilling item at ₹1 307, governs — and the three blasting items **21.17, 21.18
and 21.19** at ₹869, ₹1 033 and ₹1 322 **do not apply to this project at all**.

**The last 800 mm is the one band the schedule refuses to fix.** 157.44 m³
between (−)6.000 and (−)6.800, plus the 9.477 m³ sump pit below it, fall past
the SSR's last defined band. WM4 does not invent a percentage. Those two lines
carry the 4.5–6.0 m band's +30 % as a **declared lower bound**, tagged `[A]`,
and the question is raised as open item **WM4-V1**. Every further 10 percentage
points is about ₹21 800 on the two lines together.

## What the SSR does not contain

Six things were searched for and are simply not in the schedule:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Waterstops** | 109.76 m measured. Searched for *waterstop*, *water stop*, *water bar* and *PVC water bar* across all 624 pages — **no item exists** |
| **Spiral stair** | No item. SSR 40.06, an SS 304 handrail at ₹1 220/m, is the only related item and cannot stand for a stair |
| **Turfing** | The SSR directs Parks and Gardens wing rates, which this project does not hold. The 300 topsoil layer itself *is* priced, at 21.36, because it re-uses the material stripped at E-01a |
| **Armoured vision panels** | Not a schedule item |
| **EMP and shielding** | Nothing in chapters 41–43, or anywhere else |
| **Blast doors, hatches, valves, NBC trains, generator** | Nothing |

The schedule answers this itself, in Section B of the General Notes:

> *The items for which rates are not included in State Schedule of Rates, the
> rates shall be approved by concerned Superintending Engineer, PWD.*

That is the route for all of them, and it is recorded as open item **WM4-V7**
rather than filled with a number.

## The owner's own bill, checked against the schedule

Master H.15 records of the owner's priced bill: *"No cost was re-estimated, no
rate was checked against a market or a schedule of rates."* WM4 is that check.
Their quantities and their rates are reproduced exactly as supplied and
**nothing in their bill is edited**.

Of 37 lines, **21** have an SSR item that can stand against them.
On those lines:

| | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Owner's rates | ₹ 10,986,464 |
| SSR 2022-23 | ₹ 14,454,895 |
| **Difference** | **₹ 3,468,431  (+31.6 %)** |

The gap is concentrated in three places, and each has a reason:

* **Casting 600 mm perimeter and shear walls (M35)** — 132.61 m3 at Rs 8,640 against SSR Rs 16,024.97: **Rs 979,321**.
* **Mass excavation in basalt / murum (~6.8 m)** — 1,539.00 m3 at Rs 850 against SSR Rs 1,307.00: **Rs 703,323**.
* **Casting 900 mm pressure roof slab (M35)** — 114.72 m3 at Rs 8,640 against SSR Rs 14,391.00: **Rs 659,755**.

R.C.C. wall casting is the largest because wall formwork is what makes the SSR
pardi item dear, and the owner's single blended concrete rate of ₹8 640 does not
distinguish a wall from a raft. Rock excavation is second because the owner's
₹850 blends murum and basalt into one figure and carries no depth increase.
Reinforcement is third: ₹78 000 against the SSR's ₹89 703 for TMT Fe-500 fixed
in position.

**None of this makes the owner's bill wrong.** A rate below schedule is a
commercial position, not an error. What WM4 supplies is the comparison that did
not exist, line by line, so the position can be taken knowingly.

## What was verified, and how

* **18 automated consistency checks, 18 pass.** They prove that every WM1 line
  split to reach two SSR items sums back to the WM1 quantity exactly — the
  excavation bands, the headhouse walls against its roof, the sentry beams
  across two levels, the painting split — and that the reinforcement net weight
  is exactly the WM1 order quantity divided by 1.05.
* **Every rate re-read from the PDF a second time**, against the raw text of
  the page it sits on. 30 of 33 matched first time; three were checked by hand
  and **two were corrected** (21.40 and 39.50). Neither correction touches a
  priced line.
* **All 203 workbook formulas evaluated** and the workbook's own arithmetic
  shown to reproduce the bill — `Scripts/wm4_verify_xlsx.py`.
* **The grade-uplift formula checked against the schedule's own published
  steps** in four item families before being used where the schedule stops.

### What was NOT verified

* **No analysis was run.** This is a rating exercise. No `.std` file was opened
  and no STAAD.Pro run took place.
* **The quantities were not re-checked.** They are WM1's, and WM1's own 65-check
  audit covers them.
* **No district cost index was applied.** The SSR is a state schedule and its
  circular gives each Superintending Engineer power to vary rates for local
  conditions. No Pune circle variation exists in this project — **WM4-V4**.
